paragraphs.text: Right-click spelling suggestions in the DeepSeek Harness composer: ranked corrections, add to dictio
nary, and the standard edit actions.

# Composer spellcheck
Right-click a word in the message composer and get spelling suggestions, with

the
usual editing commands in the same menu.
## Install

The browser half is prebuilt and committed (`client.js`), so there is no build
step and no network a

is prebuilt and committed (`client.js`), so there is no build
step and no network access at runtime.

1. In the app, open the plugin manager (Settings → Plugins) and install from a
local folder, pointin

g at a checkout of this repository.
2. Reload the window (`Ctrl+R`). The browser half is loaded per

page load, so the
menu only appears after a reload.

For scripted installs, `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <path-or-git-url>`
installs the package half

; the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list also needs
this package (the plugin manager does both ste

e profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list also needs
this package (the plugin manager does both steps).
## What it does

- Adds a **capture-phase `contextmenu` listener** on `document`. It only claims
events whose target

sits inside the composer (`[data-composer-input]`, the
Lexical editor), so every other right-click i

n the app behaves exactly as
before.
- Works out the word under the pointer, checks it against a bun

dled dictionary,
and opens the shared Web context menu (`ctx.contextMenus`) with:
1. up to five sugg

estions, ranked by edit distance and then word frequency;
2. **Add to dictionary** — remembered in `

elect all, Undo, Redo**, so the
default menu functions the shell would otherwise offer are still ava

ilable.
- A word that is already known still gets the editing block, so the menu is
useful for corre

ct text too. Words the dictionary cannot match show
“No suggestions” plus the same editing commands.
- Suggestions keep the original capitalisation: `Recieve` → `Receive`.

The composer is a Lexical editor; Chromium's own squiggles are untouched. This
plugin supplies the m

enu that makes them actionable in the desktop shell, which
has no native context menu at all.
## Files
| Path | Purpose |

| `index.js` | Host half — no service, exists so the Loader entry mounts. |
| `client.js` | Built br

owser half: listener, suggestion engine, menu contribution. |
| `src/client.template.js` | Source te

mplate with `__WORDS__` / `__EXTRA__` / `__DROP__` / `__TYPOS__` placeholders. |
| `src/allowlist.tx

t` | Extra known words for technical writing (one per line). |
| `src/typos.json` | Curated misspell

ing → correction pairs, including typed contractions (`dont` → `don't`). |
| `tools/prepare-words.mj

s` | Downloads the frequency list once into `.tmp/`, filters and writes `.tmp/words.json`. |
| `tool

s/build-client.mjs` | Injects the word data into the template and writes `client.js`. |
| `tools/tes
t-client.mjs` | Loads the built bundle through a stub loader, applies it to a fake `contextMenus`, a
nd checks suggestions and timing. |
## Rebuild
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`prepare-words.mjs` downloads the frequency list once into `.tmp/` (git-ignored);
the other two scri

pts need nothing beyond Node.js, so a fresh clone can rebuild
`client.js` offline.
Reload the app window afterwards; the browser half is loaded per page load.
## Dictionary

`~30k` words from the FrequencyWords
English list (CC-BY-SA), plus the allowlist, plus the curated c

orrections.
Informal spellings that the corpus contains (`dont`, `cant`, `youre`, …) are
dropped, be

cause the curated map treats them as misspellings and they would
otherwise never get suggestions.
## Limits

- Only the composer is covered. Menu entries appear at the pointer; the menu
itself is the app's sha

red Web menu, so keyboard navigation and dismissal are
the platform's.
- Suggestions come from the b

undled dictionary, not from the operating
system's spellchecker, so the set of underlined words and

the set of words
with suggestions can differ slightly.
## License
MIT — see LICENSE.

The bundled word list comes from
FrequencyWords, which is
distributed under CC-BY-SA; the curated mi

sspelling table in `src/typos.json` is
original to this project.
